tasks.description: grok-cli and Helix speak different OKF protocols today; define ONE canonical v1 contract and contract-test both clients against it.
tasks.details: 2026-10-04 FINDING (John's Drive upload): the 'OKF server software' is byte-identical to Helix's own src/okf/ module — there is no standalone server. KEY INSIGHT: Helix was designed to BE its own OKF server: src/io/web_server/mod.rs already mounts /okf/status, /okf/registry, /okf/health, /okf/schema, POST /okf/webhook (public) and POST /okf/reload, /okf/reload/force, /okf/manifest (protected), gated on [helix.okf] enabled (default false). BUT Helix's own fetcher (src/okf/fetcher.rs) requests endpoints the server does NOT mount: GET /okf/manifest.json, GET /okf/bundles/{id}/manifest.json, GET /okf/knowledge/{kid}. So Helix cannot serve itself — the server half and client half disagree on paths. The v1 protocol MUST reconcile the mounted routes with what the fetcher (and grok-cli) expect; do not design in a vacuum. GROUND TRUTH (verified 2026-10-04 against actual code): the two OKF clients were built against different imagined servers. Helix (src/okf/fetcher.rs) expects: GET {base}/okf/manifest.json, GET {base}/okf/bundles/{id}/manifest.json, GET {base}/okf/knowledge/{kid}, GET {base}/okf/health, optional Bearer auth_token, ETag/If-None-Match. grok-cli expects: POST {http(s)}://{server}:{port}/api/traces (default port 8080, 10s timeout, buffer-on-failure; src/workflow/okf.rs), POST {remote_url}/bundles/{bundle}/concepts (15s timeout; src/tools/okf_tools.rs push_concept_to_remote). grok-cli has NO remote fetch; Helix has NO push/trace. No single server satisfies both. CANONICAL v1 PROPOSAL (minimizes churn — Helix reads stay as-is): GET /okf/health -> 200 {"status":"ok"}; GET /okf/manifest.json and GET /okf/bundles/{id}/manifest.json -> manifest matching okf_bundle_schema.json (required: id, version); GET /okf/knowledge/{kid} -> document; POST /okf/traces (JSON WorkflowTrace, was grok-cli /api/traces); POST /okf/bundles/{bundle}/concepts (JSON OkfConcept, was grok-cli /bundles/{b}/concepts). Optional Bearer auth on all; ETag/If-None-Match on GETs; JSON error bodies {"error": ...}. WORK: write PROTOCOL.md (repo root or src/okf/) documenting every endpoint with request/response examples; update any Helix paths that deviate; grok-cli retarget is task grok-cli#480 (cross-repo — coordinate, do not duplicate). Contract tests: mock HTTP server asserting exact paths, methods, auth headers, ETag round-trip, and shape conformance to okf_bundle_schema.json.

Send it on every WS connect right after the existing backends send (~line 677), and re-broadcast via state.msg_tx on every registry change (spawn/finish). Client re-renders from the snapshot — no incremental-sync state, payload is tiny (a few backends + a few subagents).

Insert at the chat_request publish site (mod.rs ~line 1116, where `llm` and `correlation_id` are both in scope). In the bridge thread, extend the forwarded ollama_response / llm_output JSON with correlation_id when present in the inner bus data, and remove the matching entry. activity = working iff any in-flight entry for that backend. tasks.title: Adaptive support-mail poll loop (15m biz / 1m burst / 30m night)
tasks.description: The SYSADMIN-01 watcher core: a persisted state machine that checks support@ on an adaptive cadence — 15 min during business hours, 1-min burst while unhandled mail exists, 30 min overnight. Driven by the existing routine system.
tasks.details:
FILED BY SURVEYOR 1, 2026-10-13. SYSADMIN-01 support-mail system, phase 2.

Definitions (normative for this task):
- Business hours: 08:00-18:00 America/New_York, from a [support] config section (business_start, business_end, timezone); defaults as stated, adjustable without code changes.
- UNHANDLED message: a support@ message with no staged draft, no sent reply, and not explicitly dismissed by John.
- QUIET: zero unhandled messages.
- BURST: entered when a check finds >=1 new unhandled message; cadence becomes every 1m. Exited after 2 consecutive clean checks (quiet_streak >= 2) -> back to time-of-day cadence.
- Normal cadence: 15m in business hours, 30m overnight.

Implementation:
1. New module src/support_watch/ (mod.rs state machine + cadence logic, state.rs persisted JSON: last_check_ms, mode, quiet_streak, last_seen_uid, unhandled_count). State file lives with other runtime state (same dir as routines JSON) so restarts don't lose it; add it to scripts/backup-state.sh (task 244).
2. Tick driver: register routine id "support-mail-watch", schedule "every 1m", enabled, at startup in the cron registry (src/cron/registry.rs pattern). The 1m tick consults state: only performs a real mailbox check when now - last_check >= current desired cadence. (One routine + internal state machine, NOT three routines toggled on/off — that races.)
3. Mailbox check uses mcp__mail__* tools (names per task 255.3; resolve defensively). New messages since last_seen_uid -> mark unhandled, enter burst, hand each to the draft flow (task 257/258).
4. Orchestration runs IN the Helix process on the R630 — no LLM needed for check/state decisions; do NOT spawn an LLM just to poll.
5. Inbound mail is untrusted: it already flows through the task-235 injection tagging (security::maybe_tag wraps mcp results in tools::execute) — verify this covers the new call sites and note it in code comments.
6. Log every check at info level (time, cadence, new count, mode transitions) so John can audit the loop from logs.

TZ), restart persistence round-trip, no-check when interval not elapsed. Integration test with stub mcp__mail__* tools. No test may require the real mail-mcp binary or network.
